summary: Ship: no S1 and no S2. I read all 12 site files and opened all 8 screenshots. I also played the page in real Chromium 141 through Playwright, using about 17 throwaway scripts under /home/user/sonnet-every-day/work/2026-10-12/qa/critic-tmp/. The static server is stopped. report.json ok=true with no errors. My own runs also had 0 console errors, 0 page errors and 0 non-local requests, apart from the errors I provoked on purpose (blocked game.js, no 2D canvas). The CSP is byte-identical to ops/templates/page-shell.html. Loaded payload is 201,023 bytes against the 250 KB budget, and the DOM has 276 nodes. There are no inline handlers or forms, one module script, every id from SPEC 4.6 is present, and all JS passes the syntax check. I re-ran test/selftest.mjs: ok, exit 0, T1 to T4 pass in 9.6 s. That backs the making-of sentences (chunks 1, 7 and 60; minimum gleam 96.2 percent on 365 rinks...

scores.note: A forward-only machine with a 10 ft turning radius, one water tank with a refill door, five seeded mishaps and a grade built from gleam, tidy, time and bumps. Selftest T3: spiral beats mow by 56 median points on 100 seeds, so strategy matters. Watch a lap teaches it and the daily seed plus challenge hash give a reason to return.

Selftest: 27 determinism runs with 0 mismatches (chunks 1, 7, 60 and a golden digest), 365 rinks winnable (min 96.2 percent), 2,000 hostile hashes. In-browser: 18 hostile hashes, denied and corrupt localStorage, blocked game.js, audio and postcard, no 2D canvas, about 450 random clicks and keys, resize loops and hidden-tab pause all gave 0 console or page errors. Only quirks are bot-lap labelling and focus-versus-Enter.

Cozy paper-ice palette, crisp rink drawing with scars distinguished by shape and luminance, hazard-striped low-water gauge, a glowing spoiler-safe postcard, and dark mode that matches. Slightly busy diagonal gloss hatching and a generic chip HUD keep it from 9.

Feedback on every action: sheen film, predicted turning arcs, toasts plus live region, stamp animation, sparkle, buff sweep and confetti, bump shake, hat wobble. Sound is muted by default with a visible toggle and works with no errors. Hover and touch aim steers proportionally. Reduced-motion twins verified: attract frozen, shake off, 0 running animations. I could not judge the audio itself by ear.

Separate portrait (rotated rink) and desktop layouts. Contract viewports pass and so do 320x640, 768x1024 and 1920x1080, with no overflow at 320 even with About and the dialog open. Contrast minimum 5.15 in light, 14 tab stops all with focus rings, meter role, live region, 44 px targets. Gaps: landscape phones (d05), Enter after click (d07), silent seed error (d09).

Dry rink-crew voice ('Boards. The machine does not enjoy that.'), units on numbers, mishaps labelled invented, rink labelled stylized, nine sources identical to project.json and dated. NHL date and the steering story were re-confirmed by my own searches. The maker's name appears only inside citation URLs. Deductions: clean laps undefined, bot laps unlabelled, one undated prior-art sentence.

201 KB loaded, 276 DOM nodes, 0 non-local requests, CSP identical to the shell, heap flat over 40 restarts. Desktop 60 fps (p99 16.8 ms); JS is about 1 percent of a profile. Static states still repaint every frame (about 40 percent main thread in software raster), and a 4x-throttled DPR 3 phone ran about 30 fps.

The first frame is a half-gleaming wrecked rink with a demo lap and a glossy sheen trail, and the 1200x630 composition matches DESIGN (rink about 984 px wide, chips and Demo lap chip on one row, Start in view). Result card, postcard, copy strip, challenge hash and a Save card PNG download (between-periods-qa1.png) all work. Share buttons sit below the fold in the 1366x768 dialog (d06).

highlights: The wet-ice sheen delivers the headline moment. A bright film trails the machine, the stripe dries to white mirror gloss and the scars vanish under it, with predicted turning arcs and an aim reticle on top. The half-gleaming demo frame is the thumbnail and it sells the page at once.

The water mechanic is legible through several channels. Under 25 percent the gauge turns hazard-striped, the coach line says 'Water is low', and the live region announces it (observed at tick 1744). At empty the gauge goes red with a drop-slash icon, a red dashed ring circles the machine and a toast fires (tick 2316), and gleam really stops growing while the tank is dry.

It is provably fair. Selftest: 27 determinism runs including 1, 7 and 60 tick chunking with a golden digest, all 365 daily rinks winnable (minimum 96.2 percent gleam), spiral beats mow by 56 median points, and plus or minus 3 degrees of jitter costs at most one grade band. The making-of's test claims are true.

The result card is something you would send. A rubber-stamp grade, a glowing spoiler-safe postcard of your own route that never shows the scars, a ten-square copy strip, a challenge hash (#s=qa1&c=D-23) that reloads as a banner, and Save card downloads between-periods-qa1.png.

Defensive engineering. 18 hostile hashes fall back to today's rink with a kind toast, denied or corrupt localStorage gives one polite note, blocked audio or postcard modules disable only themselves, a canvas-less browser gets a readable boot error, and about 450 random clicks and keys plus resize and hidden-tab pause produced no console errors.

Voice and honesty. Mishaps are labelled invented, the rink is stylized with no printed dimensions, sources are dated 'as of 2026-10-12', and the maker's name appears only inside citation URLs. The NHL opening date, the steering-jam story and the existence of a prior browser doodle and a commercial game were all re-confirmed by independent searches.

defects.title: Buttons overlap text on short laptop windows
defects.detail: Not caused by this loop: the original build/site renders the same rects. The first QA pass missed it because it measured 1366x768, 1280x800 and 1200x630 but never a window 1280 px or wider and under 720 px tall. From 1280 px up the stylesheet makes .rk-below a two-column grid (minmax(0,1fr) minmax(340px,440px)) whose width follows the rink (--rk-w). On a short window the rink shrinks to 560-730 px, so the dock column is only 146-250 px wide, and .rk-bar (flex: 0 0 auto from 768 px up) cannot shrink or wrap. Practice, Slow, Call it, Again and Result spill into the .rk-more column and sit under or over Watch a lap, the seed row and the rink-info and Best lines: the first screen looks broken...
defects.evidence: Chromium 141, light, no touch. (a) 1366x600, #s=qa1, ready: document.elementFromPoint at the centre of #btn-practice (x 561-734, y 552-596) returns #btn-watch (overlap 4,084 px2; .rk-watch is x 565-1005, y 538-582); the screenshot shows Watch a lap drawn over Practice (no clock). Press Enter: #btn-slow (x 503-601, y 551-595) is covered by #best (x 539-979, y 567-585) and #rink-info. (b) 1280x650, #s=qa1&c=D-99999 (challenge link), playing: #btn-finish (x 562-639, y 601-645) has its centre (60...
defects.suggestedFix: In css/style.css section 9, change the block that opens with '@media (min-width: 1280px) {' (it sets .rk-below to the two-column grid, .rk-more to a column, .rk-seed, .rk-dock wrap and .rk-coach) to '@media (min-width: 1280px) and (min-height: 720px) {', so windows shorter than 720 px keep the stacked layout that already works from 768 to 1279 px. I tried exactly this in a scratch copy: 56 cells (1280, 1366, 1536 and 1920 wide by 560 to 720 tall, plain and challenge) had no covered or overlap...

defects.title: Share text box cuts its own text on phones
defects.detail: Side effect of the d06 fix: '@media (max-width: 767px) { .rk-share { height: 5rem } }'. On a phone the four-line share text wraps to about seven lines (142 px) but the box is 76 px high, so the strip of squares is cut through the middle and the link line is hidden. The original box was 121 px, which also clipped, but by only 21 px. The tighter dialog also leaves a few phone and short-window cases with the share row under the sticky bar at open. The laptop case (d06) is fixed and not affected.
defects.evidence: 390x844 light touch, #s=qa1: tap Start, Call it, dialog opens: #share-text clientHeight 76, scrollHeight 142 (same at 360x640, 375x667, 320x568; build/site: 121 and 142). Screenshot /home/user/sonnet-every-day/work/2026-10-12/qa/critic-tmp/recheck/shots/new-open-390x844-timed.png shows the half-cut row of squares. 390x844 with #s=qa1&c=D-99999: dialog scrollHeight 832, clientHeight 806, Save card y 731-775 against sticky bar y 759-825 when the dialog opens (16 px hidden, a 26 px scroll reveal...
defects.suggestedFix: Make the box a whole number of lines or size it to its text, so no line is cut in half: for example in ui.js setShareText() set ta.style.height = 'auto' and then ta.style.height = ta.scrollHeight + 'px' (the dialog may scroll under the sticky bar), or keep a fixed height of 4 lines (about 6.6rem). Recover vertical space on phones elsewhere, for example a postcard cap (.rk-postcard max-height: 26dvh with object-fit: contain) and tighter .rk-stats cells (padding 4px 8px). Re-check at 390x844 wi...

defects.title: Packaged project.json still has the removed claim
defects.detail: The revise copy deleted the unverified sentence 'Earlier ice-resurfacing games exist (per our own web searches: a browser doodle from 2013 and at least one commercial game)' from index.html (d01, d02). The makingOf field of work/2026-10-12/package/project.json (the draft the packaging step copies to docs/d/<slug>/project.json) and of spec/PROJECT.json still carries it, so the published JSON would differ from the About panel (PLAYBOOK 10.1: makingOf is the same paragraph as the About panel) and would republish a claim with no verified source (my own searches could not confirm the year 2013). The gallery does not render makingOf, so this is a public metadata file only, not page copy.
defects.evidence: grep -c 2013 /home/user/sonnet-every-day/work/2026-10-12/package/project.json prints 1; the .sed-making-of paragraph in /home/user/sonnet-every-day/work/2026-10-12/tmp/revise-site/index.html contains none of '2013', 'doodle', 'commercial game' or 'own web search'. Comparison script r1-text.mjs (output r1.json): package/project.json makingOf identicalToPage false, sources identical to the page.
defects.suggestedFix: At packaging, set makingOf in package/project.json to the exact text of .sed-making-of in the final index.html (it ends '...Seeding a daily puzzle from the date is common practice (per three craft write-ups listed below).') before staging. Afterwards grep -c 2013 docs/d/2026-10-12-between-periods/project.json must print 0.

defects.title: Hard-coded placeholder date goes stale
defects.detail: The seed input has placeholder='2026-10-12' written into the markup. The field is normally filled with the current seed by ui.js, so the placeholder only shows if the visitor clears it. From tomorrow it will advertise a date that is not today's rink.
defects.evidence: index.html line 283: placeholder='2026-10-12'. Load the page, clear #seed-input: the grey hint reads 2026-10-12 regardless of today's seed.
defects.suggestedFix: Use a neutral hint such as placeholder='e.g. qa1', or set the placeholder from the seed in ui.js updateInfo().

defects.title: Toggle accessible names differ from visible labels
defects.detail: At 1500px and wider the three preference buttons show visible text 'Sound off', 'Guides on' and 'Shake on' (.rk-lab), but their accessible names are the fixed aria-label values 'Sound', 'Guides' and 'Shake'. Voice-control users who say what they see ('click Sound off') do not match the name, which is a WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name gap. Only voice control on very wide screens is affected.
defects.evidence: index.html lines 245 to 247, and css/style.css `@media (min-width: 1500px) { .rk-sq .rk-lab { display: inline } }`. At 1600x900 the visible text is 'Sound off' while the accessible name is 'Sound'.
defects.suggestedFix: Make the visible text constant ('Sound', 'Guides', 'Shake') and rely on aria-pressed plus the icon swap for state. That matches the aria-label exactly and also avoids announcing 'Sound off, pressed'.

defects.title: Canvas repaints every frame even when static
defects.detail: game.js calls the frame callbacks on every animation frame and render.js drawFrame() repaints the whole canvas each time, even when nothing changes (paused, result dialog open, reduced-motion frozen demo). JS cost is tiny, but the continuous native repaint keeps the main thread busy in software-raster Chromium. This is not a defect on GPU hardware I could not test; it is a cheap battery and CPU win.
defects.evidence: 1366x768, DPR 1, CDP Performance TaskDuration over 3 s. Attract 39 percent, playing 41, paused 39, result dialog open 38; with reduced motion on, the frozen attract frame still reads 38 and the dialog 40. A 3 s CPU profile of the paused page: idle 57 percent, '(program)' native 41 percent, all JS about 25 ms, which is about 1 percent. At DPR 2 the main thread is about 99 percent busy. A 390x844 DPR 3 profile under 4x CPU throttle gave p50 33 ms and p95 50 ms frame gaps. Desktop unthrottled st...
defects.suggestedFix: In render.js draw(), early-out when nothing changed. Keep a signature of canvas client size, DPR, palette, view.gridVersion, view.tick, machine pose, phase, prefs.assist and aim, and skip the repaint when the phase is paused, done, or ready with reduced motion, no shake, sparkle, buff or confetti is active, and fresh.n is 0. Always repaint on resize or a colour-scheme change.

defects.title: Prior-art line lacks date, year unverified
defects.detail: The making-of paragraph says 'Earlier ice-resurfacing games exist (per our own web searches: a browser doodle from 2013 and at least one commercial game)'. That sentence carries no 'as of' date, while the 'Real and made up' section does. The claim is honestly attributed and search-only, as the spec allowed. My own search on 2026-10-12 corroborates that a browser doodle and a paid Xbox/Windows title exist, but none of my snippets shows the year 2013, so the year is unverifiable from our network.
defects.evidence: index.html line 331 (making-of) versus line 339 ('...per our own web searches, as of 2026-10-12'). WebSearch 'ice resurfacing machine browser game': results list a Google Zamboni doodle with no year in the snippet and a commercial title; no snippet shows 2013.
defects.suggestedFix: Reword to 'a browser doodle and at least one commercial game, per our own web searches, as of 2026-10-12' and drop 2013 unless a source with that year is found. Update the matching sentence in PROJECT.json makingOf and the packaged project.json in the same change, because the integrator keeps both identical (they are identical today).

defects.title: Bot lap wording survives in live text and coach
defects.detail: d04 relabelled the result card, the postcard and the copied text, but two lines still read as the player's own result after a bot lap: the live-region announcement and the coach line under the rink (the engineer saw the same). A screen-reader user, or anyone who closes the card, hears or reads a grade stamp line for a lap the bot drove.
defects.evidence: 1366x768, #s=qa1&a=mow: when the card opens #live reads 'Grade S, Mirror. Skate-ready. Nobody can tell you were here. 93.9 percent gleam, 2,464 feet.' and #coach reads 'Skate-ready. Nobody can tell you were here.'; the HUD Grade chip shows S.
defects.suggestedFix: In ui.js coachFor() return T.botLap when v.phase === 'done' and v.result.mode === 'auto'; in the app:finish handler begin the announcement with 'Bot lap.' and leave out the grade stamp line when r.mode === 'auto'.

proofread.notes: Sandbox network looks restricted: all 9 links answered 000 once each, with no retries, so the 9 unreachable-link entries are not evidence against the sites. Otherwise no typos, leftovers or source mismatches found; the two unverified-claim entries are the 2013-doodle sentence in the About panel and the Real section. Oddities (research steering wording, Mental Floss attribution) went to kaizen/notes-clerk.md.
